a_extract.problem: The paper establishes an explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem in the plane.

bridge.rationale: Both papers tackle Erdős's unit distance problem in the plane from complementary angles: Paper A provides an explicit algebraic construction of dense unit-distance point sets using class field theory, while Paper B analyzes the structural rigidity of dense unit-distance configurations. bridge.mediator: Algebraic lattice frameworks
bridge.sketch: A researcher would construct a unit-distance graph using the projection of Golod-Shafarevich lattices as defined in Paper A, and then analyze its infinitesimal and combinatorial rigidity using the tools from Paper B. By leveraging the Galois-theoretic symmetries of the lattice, one could prove the existence of large, highly symmetric rigid sub-frameworks that are otherwise difficult to construct or analyze in generic settings. a.title: On the Minimal Denominator Problem in Function Fields

a_extract.problem: The paper investigates the probability distribution of the minimal denominator degree and the distribution of the unique monic minimal denominator polynomial in function fields.
a_extract.methods: The authors translate the minimal denominator problem into linear algebra using ranks of Hankel matrices and apply counting techniques over finite fields.

a_extract.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at the minimal denominator problem in the infinite residue case, such as over the field of rational functions with real or complex coefficients, but note that their counting techniques do not apply.

b_extract.problem: The paper aims to speed up algorithms for sparse convolution, text-to-pattern Hamming distances, and the constellation problem by reducing the overhead of mod-prime hashing.
b_extract.methods: The main technique used is the large sieve inequality from analytic number theory to analyze and improve mod-prime hash functions.
b_extract.regime: The results apply asymptotically in the standard word RAM model for sparse inputs and restricted universe sizes.
b_extract.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at generalizing the sparse general convolution algorithm to remove the restriction on the input vector length.

bridge.rationale: While Paper A focuses on algebraic properties of minimal denominators in function fields and Paper B focuses on algorithmic sparse convolution via the large sieve, they are connected by the algebraic structure of Hankel matrices, which represent convolution systems. The large sieve inequality has well-known analogues in function fields that could be used to bound the distribution of Hankel matrix ranks for sparse or restricted polynomial families.
bridge.mediator: Function Field Large Sieve and Sparse Hankel Systems

By applying a function-field analogue of the large sieve inequality (similar to the analytic number theory tools in Paper B), one could bound the exceptional set of polynomials where the minimal denominator degree deviates from the expected distribution. This would provide faster randomized algorithms for recovering rational functions from sparse samples in function fields.
